claims.claim: KSHV-encoded genes include homologs of cellular genes such as vCyclin, vFLIP, vGPCR, and vIRFs.
claims.source: Many KSHV-encoded genes are also identified as homologs of cellular genes such as vCyclin, vFLIP, vGPCR, and vIRFs (Mesri et al., 2014; Giffin and Damania, 2014).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Mesri et al., 2014; Giffin and Damania, 2014).

claims.claim: Upon infection, KSHV can either enter a latent phase or continue toward lytic replication.
claims.source: Upon successful infection of host cells, the virus chooses to either enter a latent phase or continue toward lytic replication to generate more copies of infectious virions (Chandran, 2010; Nicol et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Chandran, 2010; Nicol et al., 2016).

claims.claim: To establish latency, the KSHV genome undergoes epigenetic modifications predominantly at lysine residues on histones.
claims.source: To establish latency, the viral genome transitions through a series of epigenetic modifications that are predominantly at lysine residues on histones to minimize expression of the majority of encoded genes. Only a fraction of genes critical for latency is expressed (Uppal et al., 2015; Toth et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Uppal et al., 2015; Toth et al., 2010).

claims.claim: Major KSHV-encoded genes expressed in KSHV-positive cancer biopsy samples include LANA, vCyclin, vFLIP, and vIRFs.
claims.source: The major KSHV-encoded genes expressed in the majority of KSHV-positive cancer biopsy samples include the latency-associated nuclear antigen (LANA), the virus encoded homolog of human cyclin D (vCyclin), the homolog of FLICE-like inhibitory protein (vFLIP) and homologs of Interferon regulatory factors (vIRF1, vIRF2, vIRF3, and vIRF4) (Arias et al., 2014; Damania, 2004).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Arias et al., 2014; Damania, 2004).

claims.claim: KSHV-positive biopsy samples have transcripts for vGPCR and glycoprotein K8.
claims.source: Additionally, KSHV-positive biopsy samples are also known to have transcripts for the human homolog of the G-protein-coupled receptor (vGPCR) and glycoprotein K8 (Arias et al., 2014; Damania, 2004).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Arias et al., 2014; Damania, 2004).

claims.claim: LANA plays an essential role in maintenance of KSHV episomes by tethering KSHV DNA to the host genome.
claims.source: KSHV-encoded LANA plays an essential role in maintenance of KSHV episomes within the host by tethering the KSHV DNA to the host genome (Uppal et al., 2014; Cotter and Robertson, 1999; Ballestas et al., 1999).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Uppal et al., 2014; Cotter and Robertson, 1999; Ballestas et al., 1999).

claims.claim: LANA-mediated KSHV genome persistence requires its C-terminal binding to KSHV DNA and N-terminal binding to host nuclear DNA.
claims.source: LANA-mediated KSHV genome persistence requires its C-terminal, which binds to the KSHV DNA within its terminal repeat region while the N-terminal region of LANA binds with the host nuclear DNA (Schwam et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Schwam et al., 2000).

claims.claim: LANA regulates cell cycle, apoptosis, EMT, and chromosome instability.
claims.source: The major pathways modulated by KSHV-encoded LANA include cell cycle (Wei et al., 2016), apoptosis (Friborg et al., 1999), Epithelial-Mesenchymal transition (EMT) (Gasperini et al., 2012; Jha et al., 2016), and chromosome instability (CIN) (Lang et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Wei et al., 2016; Friborg et al., 1999; Gasperini et al., 2012; Jha et al., 2016; Lang et al., 2018).

claims.claim: KSHV-encoded vCyclin facilitates G1/S transition and overrides contact inhibition.
claims.source: KSHV-encoded vCyclin is a homolog of host Cyclin D and is known to facilitate the G1/S transition and override contact inhibition of viral-infected cells (Jones et al., 2014; Verschuren et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Jones et al., 2014; Verschuren et al., 2002).

claims.claim: vFLIP targets the NF-kB pathway to promote oncogenesis.
claims.source: Another latent antigen vFLIP is known to target the NF-kB pathway to promote oncogenesis (Sun and Cesarman, 2011; Zhao et al., 2015; Rahman and McFadden, 2011).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Sun and Cesarman, 2011; Zhao et al., 2015; Rahman and McFadden, 2011).

claims.claim: vIRFs can inhibit pro-apoptotic pathways mediated by the BH3-family of proteins.
claims.source: Similarly, vIRFs can inhibit pro-apoptotic pathways such as those mediated by the BH3-family of proteins (Choi et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Choi et al., 2012).

claims.claim: vGPCR is expressed in KSHV positive-tumor biopsy samples.
claims.source: KSHV-encoded vGPCR, considered to be a lytic gene, was also shown to be expressed in a number of KSHV positive-tumor biopsy samples (Damania, 2004).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Damania, 2004).

claims.claim: vGPCR regulates MAPK pathway activity through p38 and upregulates HIF1α.
claims.source: It was shown to be a bonafide oncoprotein, that regulates activities of the MAPK pathway through p38 and upregulation of the hypoxia survival protein HIF1α (Montaner et al., 2013; Vischer et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Montaner et al., 2013; Vischer et al., 2014).

claims.claim: TPA and Butyric acid are effective inducers of in-vitro reactivation of KSHV from latently-infected cells.
claims.source: Hence, the use of 12-O-tetradecanoylphorbol-13-acetate (TPA) and Butyric acid (BA), potent epigenetic modifiers, are effective inducers of in-vitro reactivation of KSHV from latently-infected cells.
claims.evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about TPA/BA as epigenetic modifiers and KSHV reactivation inducers.

claims.claim: Exposure of KSHV positive cells to hypoxia or reactive oxygen species can induce KSHV reactivation.
claims.source: In addition to epigenetic modulation by TPA/BA, exposure of KSHV positive cells to hypoxia or reactive oxygen species can induce KSHV reactivation (Ye et al., 2011a; Aneja and Yuan, 2017; Davis et al., 2001; Cai et al., 2006a; Ye et al., 2011b).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Ye et al., 2011a; Aneja and Yuan, 2017; Davis et al., 2001; Cai et al., 2006a; Ye et al., 2011b).

claims.claim: Hypoxia is detrimental to aerobic cells by dramatically reducing ATP generation through oxidative phosphorylation.
claims.source: Hypoxia is detrimental to aerobic cells depriving them of energy supplies due to the dramatic drop in their ability to generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation.
claims.evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about cellular metabolism and hypoxia effects.

claims.claim: The adaptive response to hypoxia includes arrest of cell cycle at G1/S transition and DNA replication.
claims.source: The adaptive response to hypoxia includes arrest of cell cycle, mainly at G1/S transition, and DNA replication due to a loss of available cellular energy stores, and the macromolecular complexes that drive these processes (Mason and Rathmell, 2011; Michiels, 2004).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Mason and Rathmell, 2011; Michiels, 2004).

claims.claim: HIFs are stabilized in hypoxia to activate transcription of stress-associated genes.
claims.source: In hypoxia, the specialized transcription factors (Hypoxia inducible factors; HIFs) are stabilized to activate transcription of stress-associated genes responsible for metabolic reprogramming, survival, angiogenesis, and anti-apoptosis (Dengler et al., 2014; Majmundar et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Dengler et al., 2014; Majmundar et al., 2010).

claims.claim: Stabilization of HIF1α arrests G1/S transition through regulation of p21 and p27.
claims.source: Nevertheless, stabilization of HIF1α is known for arresting G1/S transition through regulation of the cyclin dependent kinase inhibitors p21 and p27, and other related pathways (Gardner et al., 2001; Hammond et al., 2002; Goda et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Gardner et al., 2001; Hammond et al., 2002; Goda et al., 2003).

claims.claim: KSHV utilizes multiple mechanisms to maintain a high basal level of HIF1α in infected cells.
claims.source: KSHV, like other oncogenic viruses, utilizes multiple mechanisms to maintain a high basal level of HIF1α in infected cells and infected cells are adjusted to survive with higher HIF1α levels as evident from their normal proliferation and replication potential.
claims.evidence: Based on inference from the observation that KSHV-infected cells maintain normal proliferation despite high HIF1α levels.

claims.claim: The KSHV genome undergoes enhanced lytic replication upon induction of hypoxia.
claims.source: Paradoxically, the KSHV genome in infected cells undergoes enhanced lytic replication upon further induction of hypoxia through their ability to bypass HIF1α-mediated block to DNA replication.
claims.evidence: Based on established knowledge about KSHV reactivation in hypoxia and inference about bypassing HIF1α-mediated blocks.

claims.claim: KSHV-encoded vCyclin physically interacts with HIF1α and abrogates its transcriptional activity.
claims.source: Specifically, KSHV-encoded vCyclin expressed in hypoxia physically interacts with HIF1α and abrogates its transcriptional activity by mediating its degradation through a non-canonical lysosomal pathway.
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data showing vCyclin-HIF1α interaction, reduced HIF1α transcriptional activity, and lysosomal degradation.

claims.claim: Knock-down of vCyclin results in compromised potential of KSHV-positive cells to bypass hypoxia-mediated suppression of DNA replication.
claims.source: Knock-down of vCyclin resulted in a compromised potential of KSHV-positive cells to bypass hypoxia-mediated suppression of DNA replication, as well as their potential to proliferate in an anchorage-dependent or independent manner.
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data showing reduced replication and proliferation in vCyclin knockdown cells.

claims.claim: KSHV-infected cells show elevated levels of HIF1α but replicate and divide spontaneously.
claims.source: KSHV infected cells show the signature of a hypoxic microenvironment with elevated levels of HIF1α, although they replicate and divide spontaneously (Cuninghame et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Cuninghame et al., 2014).

claims.claim: Introduction of external hypoxia to KSHV positive cells reactivates the virus resulting in lytic replication.
claims.source: Further, introduction of external hypoxia to KSHV positive cells is known to reactivate the virus resulting in induction of lytic replication (Davis et al., 2001; Cai et al., 2006a).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Davis et al., 2001; Cai et al., 2006a).

claims.claim: HIF1α is one of the major effectors of hypoxia and mediates repression of DNA replication in hypoxic conditions.
claims.source: As HIF1α is one of the major effectors of hypoxia and mediates repression of DNA replication in hypoxic conditions, we investigated the protein levels of HIF1α in BJAB/BJAB-KSHV cells grown in hypoxia (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about HIF1α function in hypoxia.

claims.claim: BJAB-KSHV cells were characterized for typical characteristics of latently infected KSHV-positive cells.
claims.source: BJAB-KSHV cells were previously analyzed for other characteristics of latently infected KSHV-positive cells (Singh et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Singh et al., 2018).

claims.claim: BJAB and BJAB-KSHV cells are isogenic based on STR profiling.
claims.source: These cell lines were characterized for their isogenic background through short tandem repeats (STR) profiling (Singh et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Singh et al., 2018).

claims.claim: KSHV-encoded vGPCR is a known positive regulator of HIF1α.
claims.source: Also, the KSHV-encoded vGPCR, a known positive regulator of HIF1α showed fold changes in expression of LDHA, P4HA1, and PDK1 in vGPCR transfected cells to be 1.43, 1.87, and 1.9 as compared to mock transfected cells, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data showing increased HIF1α target expression with vGPCR and established knowledge about vGPCR function.

claims.claim: GFP-vCyclin shows predominantly nuclear localization at 24 hr and cytosolic localization at 48 hr post-transfection.
claims.source: Interestingly, initial investigation for the expression of GFP-vCyclin showed a variable localization of GFP signals in both nuclear and cytosolic compartments. In the initial 24 hr, the GFP signals were predominantly localized to nuclear compartments while at a later 48 hr time, localization to the outer cytosolic compartment as punctate signals were observed (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by microscopy data showing temporal changes in vCyclin localization (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).

claims.claim: vCyclin interacts with HIF1α in naturally infected KSHV positive cells (BC3, BCBL1, and JSC1).
claims.source: We further validated the interaction between vCyclin and HIF1α in physiologically relevant, naturally infected KSHV positive cells (BC3, BCBL1, and JSC1), which were used in immuno-precipitation assays. BJAB, a KSHV negative cell line was also included as a control. The results clearly demonstrated that KSHV-encoded vCyclin interacts with HIF1α in KSHV-positive cells (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunoprecipitation data from naturally infected cells (Figure 3D).

claims.claim: Levels of GFP-vCyclin gradually decrease and are eventually lost even under antibiotic selection.
claims.source: Interestingly, we observed that in contrast to mock transfected cells, signals for vCyclin as monitored by GFP gradually decreased and eventually were lost even under antibiotics selection (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: Supported by microscopy data showing loss of GFP-vCyclin signal over time (Figure 4C).

claims.claim: GFP-vCyclin levels continuously decrease with almost complete elimination at the seven day time point.
claims.source: We transfected GFP-tagged vCyclin in HEK293T cells and checked its expression at 24 hr-time point intervals. As expected, the levels of GFP (tagged to vCyclin) were continuously decreased with its almost complete elimination at the seven day time point (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by Western blot data showing temporal decrease in GFP-vCyclin (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).

claims.claim: Treatment with proteasomal inhibitor MG132 fails to protect HIF1α from vCyclin-mediated degradation.
claims.source: The results clearly showed that treatment of cells expressing vCyclin with the proteasomal inhibitor MG132 failed to protect degradation of HIF1α.
claims.evidence: Supported by Western blot data showing HIF1α degradation despite MG132 treatment.

claims.claim: Treatment with lysosomal inhibitor Chloroquine protects HIF1α from vCyclin-mediated degradation.
claims.source: However, treatment of these cells with the lysosomal inhibitor Chloroquine protected HIF1α from vCyclin-mediated degradation (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: Supported by Western blot data showing HIF1α protection with Chloroquine treatment (Figure 4D).

claims.claim: vCyclin localizes to nuclear and lysosomal compartments.
claims.source: Nevertheless, vCyclin localization was also distributed to the nuclear as well as lysosomal compartment.
claims.evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence microscopy data showing vCyclin distribution.

claims.claim: KSHV-encoded vCyclin transcripts are upregulated in BC3 cells grown under hypoxic conditions.
claims.source: We recently observed that KSHV-encoded vCyclin transcripts were upregulated in KSHV-positive BC3 cells grown under hypoxic conditions. We further corroborated these findings by using two KSHV-positive cells lines, BCBL1 and JSC1 (Singh et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Singh et al., 2018).

claims.claim: CoCl2 treatment for 8 hr prevents VHL ubiquitin-ligase mediated degradation and stabilizes HIF1α in normoxia.
claims.source: We treated these cells with the chemical mimetic of hypoxia, CoCl2 for 8 hr to prevent VHL ubiquitin-ligase mediated degradation in normoxia, and stabilization of HIF1α in those cells (Yuan et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Yuan et al., 2003) and established knowledge about CoCl2 effects.

claims.claim: Hypoxia positively upregulates expression of KSHV-encoded vCyclin in BCBL1 and JSC1 cells.
claims.source: The real-time PCR for vCyclin transcripts in these cells confirmed that hypoxia positively upregulated expression of KSHV-encoded vCyclin (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Supported by real-time PCR data showing increased vCyclin expression in hypoxia (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).

claims.claim: The vCyclin promoter contains four distinct HREs.
claims.source: The in-silico analysis of the vCyclin promoter (Ltd promoter) revealed the presence of four distinct HREs (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Supported by in-silico analysis results (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).

claims.claim: Lysosomal degradation of HIF1α occurs in naturally infected BC3 cells.
claims.source: The results clearly suggested that lysosomal degradation of HIF1α do happen in naturally infected cells.
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from BC3 cells treated with chloroquine.

claims.claim: Knock down of vCyclin allows for higher expression of HIF1α in BC3 cells.
claims.source: Furthermore, knock down of vCyclin allowed for higher expression of HIF1α (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Supported by Western blot data showing increased HIF1α in vCyclin knockdown cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).

claims.claim: HIF-1α binds with Cdc6 in hypoxia, a protein required for loading cellular helicases (MCMs) onto DNA.
claims.source: In hypoxia, HIF-1α is known to bind with Cdc6, a crucial protein required for loading cellular helicases (MCMs) onto DNA to initiate DNA replication (Hubbi et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Hubbi et al., 2013).

claims.claim: HIF1α binding to Cdc6 explains HIF1α-mediated repression of DNA replication in hypoxia.
claims.source: This also explains HIF1α-mediated repression of DNA replication in hypoxia.
claims.evidence: Based on inference from the known interaction between HIF1α and Cdc6.

claims.claim: KSHV infection was monitored by LANA immunofluorescence and confirmed by LANA western blot.
claims.source: KSHV infection was monitored by LANA immuno-fluorescence and was confirmed by LANA western blot (Figure 5A and B).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and Western blot data (Figure 5A and B).

claims.claim: During the examined period of hypoxic induction, there was likely no suppression of DNA replication through direct binding of HIF1α to the OriLyt region.
claims.source: This suggests that during the period examined for hypoxic induction, there was likely no suppression of DNA replication through direct binding of HIF1α to the OriLyt region.
claims.evidence: Based on inference from ChIP-seq data showing HIF1α enrichment away from OriLyt regions.

claims.claim: High enrichment of HIF1α on the KSHV genome indicates enhanced transcription of KSHV-encoded lytic genes required for reactivation.
claims.source: Moreover, high enrichment of HIF1α on the KSHV genome can be an indicator of enhanced transcription of KSHV-encoded lytic genes required for KSHV reactivation (Figure 5D and E).
claims.evidence: Based on inference from ChIP-seq data showing HIF1α enrichment patterns (Figure 5D and E).

claims.claim: A fourfold or greater downregulation of vCyclin was observed at the transcript level in BC3-ShvCyclin cells.
claims.source: The knock down of vCyclin was confirmed at the transcript level by real-time PCR using cDNA from ShControl or ShvCyclin transduced BC3 cells. A fourfold or greater downregulation of vCyclin was seen at the transcript level (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: Supported by real-time PCR data showing vCyclin knockdown efficiency (Figure 6B).

claims.claim: Knock-down of vCyclin adversely affects KSHV replication even under normoxic conditions.
claims.source: Interestingly, knock-down of vCyclin adversely affected replication even under normoxic conditions (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: Supported by KSHV copy number data in normoxic conditions (Figure 6C).

claims.claim: vCyclin plays a role in balancing HIF1α levels in infected cells to allow proper replication and growth under hypoxic conditions.
claims.source: These results clearly indicated a role for vCyclin in balancing HIF1α levels in infected cells to allow proper replication and growth under hypoxic conditions.
claims.evidence: Based on inference from experimental data showing effects of vCyclin knockdown on replication and growth.

claims.claim: Hypoxia represents a detrimental stress to aerobic cells and is an established physiological character of cancer and oncogenic virus infected cells.
claims.source: Hypoxia represents a detrimental stress to aerobic cells and is an established physiological character of cancer as well as oncogenic virus infected cells (Seyfried and Shelton, 2010; Noch and Khalili, 2012).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Seyfried and Shelton, 2010; Noch and Khalili, 2012).

claims.claim: Hypoxic cells pose a major challenge for patients undergoing chemotherapy and radiation therapy.
claims.source: The hypoxic cells, not only need large scale reprogramming of cellular pathways for survival, but also poses a major challenge for patients undergoing chemotherapy and radiation therapy (Raz et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Raz et al., 2014).

claims.claim: HIFs possess broad transcriptional capacity for cells grown in hypoxia.
claims.source: The well-known factors responsible for reprogramming of cellular pathways under hypoxic conditions include the hypoxia inducible factors (HIFs) which possess broad transcriptional capacity for cells grown in hypoxia (Majmundar et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Majmundar et al., 2010).

claims.claim: HIF1α is considered a rate limiting protein based on its stability under hypoxic conditions.
claims.source: HIF1α is considered a rate limiting protein based on its stability, specifically under hypoxic conditions (Majmundar et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Majmundar et al., 2010).

claims.claim: HIF1α transactivates genes involved in glucose transport, glycolysis, angiogenesis, growth and survival, and invasion and metastasis.
claims.source: When stabilized, HIF1α transactivates genes involved in, but not limited to those associated with glucose transport (GLUTs), glycolysis (HK1, HK2, ENO1, GPI, and LDHA), angiogenesis (VEGF, ENG, and LRP1), growth and survival (Cyclin G2, TGF-b, EPO, and NOS), and invasion and metastasis (KRTs, MMP2, UPAR, AMF, and PAI1) (Dengler et al., 2014; Majmundar et al., 2010; Ortiz-Barahona et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Dengler et al., 2014; Majmundar et al., 2010; Ortiz-Barahona et al., 2010).

claims.claim: HIF1α is often considered an oncogenic protein.
claims.source: Based on these broad roles of HIF1α in growth and survival, the protein is often considered an oncogenic protein (Bárdos and Ashcroft, 2004).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Bárdos and Ashcroft, 2004).

claims.claim: HIF1α protein levels are tightly regulated through proteasomal degradation by VHL or lysosomal degradation mediated by CDK2 under normoxic conditions.
claims.source: Under favorable normoxic conditions, the protein levels of HIF1α is tightly regulated through its proteasomal degradation by the tumor suppressor protein VHL or lysosomal degradation mediated by cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) (Hubbi et al., 2014; Tanimoto, 2000; Pugh and Ratcliffe, 2003).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Hubbi et al., 2014; Tanimoto, 2000; Pugh and Ratcliffe, 2003).

claims.claim: Elevated HIF1α in KSHV infected cells modulates expression of key KSHV oncogenes in an autocrine manner.
claims.source: Elevated HIF1α in KSHV infected cells is known to modulate expression of key oncogenes encoded by KSHV in an autocrine manner, in addition to transactivation of cellular genes responsible for survival, growth, proliferation, angiogenesis, and metabolic reprogramming (Ma et al., 2015; Jham and Montaner, 2010; Jham et al., 2011; Semenza, 2010; Delgado et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Ma et al., 2015; Jham and Montaner, 2010; Jham et al., 2011; Semenza, 2010; Delgado et al., 2010).

claims.claim: KSHV-encoded vGPCR effects on the p38/MAPK pathway upregulate HIF1α expression.
claims.source: KSHV-encoded vGPCR effects on the p38/MAPK pathway, and EC5S-mediated ubiquitination of the tumor suppressor VHL by KSHV-encoded LANA are extensively studied pathways which shows upregulated expression of HIF1α in KSHV-infected cells (Cai et al., 2006b; Sodhi et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Cai et al., 2006b; Sodhi et al., 2000).

claims.claim: LANA-mediated EC5S ubiquitination of VHL upregulates HIF1α expression in KSHV-infected cells.
claims.source: KSHV-encoded vGPCR effects on the p38/MAPK pathway, and EC5S-mediated ubiquitination of the tumor suppressor VHL by KSHV-encoded LANA are extensively studied pathways which shows upregulated expression of HIF1α in KSHV-infected cells (Cai et al., 2006b; Sodhi et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Cai et al., 2006b; Sodhi et al., 2000).

claims.claim: HIF1α upregulates vGPCR in a cyclic manner to maintain elevated levels of HIF1α.
claims.source: HIF1α also upregulates vGPCR in a cyclic manner to maintain continued elevated levels of HIF1α, and targeting HIF1α in KSHV infected cells has been proposed as a potential therapeutic strategy against KSHV-mediated oncogenesis (Singh et al., 2018; Shrestha et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Singh et al., 2018; Shrestha et al., 2017).

claims.claim: Targeting HIF1α in KSHV infected cells has been proposed as a potential therapeutic strategy against KSHV-mediated oncogenesis.
claims.source: HIF1α also upregulates vGPCR in a cyclic manner to maintain continued elevated levels of HIF1α, and targeting HIF1α in KSHV infected cells has been proposed as a potential therapeutic strategy against KSHV-mediated oncogenesis (Singh et al., 2018; Shrestha et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Singh et al., 2018; Shrestha et al., 2017).

claims.claim: HIF1α-mediated inhibition of cell cycle progression and DNA replication depends on both transcriptional and non-transcriptional activity of HIF1α.
claims.source: It is noteworthy that hypoxia or elevated HIF1α levels induces arrest of cell cycle and DNA replication to minimize energy utilization as well as the macromolecular demands on cells, and this arrest is crucial for survival until favorable conditions return. Nevertheless, HIF1α-mediated inhibition of cell cycle progression and DNA replication depends on both transcriptional, as well as non-transcriptional activity of HIF1α (Gardner et al., 2001; Hammond et al., 2002; Goda et al., 2003; Hubbi et al., 2013; Box and Demetrick, 2004; Green et al., 2001; Martin et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Gardner et al., 2001; Hammond et al., 2002; Goda et al., 2003; Hubbi et al., 2013; Box and Demetrick, 2004; Green et al., 2001; Martin et al., 2012).

claims.claim: KSHV-infected cells divide and replicate in hypoxia and are induced to productive (lytic) replication.
claims.source: Paradoxically, in contrast to healthy cells with arrested cell cycle and DNA replication, KSHV-infected cells not only divide and replicate in hypoxia, but is induced to productive (lytic) replication (Davis et al., 2001; Cai et al., 2006a; Gardner et al., 2001; Goda et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Davis et al., 2001; Cai et al., 2006a; Gardner et al., 2001; Goda et al., 2003).

claims.claim: BJAB and BJAB-KSHV cells have similar passage numbers.
claims.source: Additionally, BJAB-KSHV cells were checked for typical characteristics of latently infected KSHV-positive cells and a similar passage number of cells were used in this study to rule out any further constraints (Singh et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Stated as a methodological control to ensure experimental validity.

claims.claim: BJAB-KSHV cells are adjusted for growth with higher levels of HIF1α and show the same growth pattern as KSHV-negative BJAB cells in normoxic conditions.
claims.source: This result suggested that BJAB-KSHV cells were adjusted for growth with higher levels of HIF1α and show the same growth pattern as KSHV-negative BJAB cells in normoxic conditions.
claims.evidence: Based on inference from experimental data showing similar growth patterns despite different HIF1α levels.

claims.claim: The presence of KSHV negatively regulates the transcriptional activity of HIF1α in hypoxic conditions to provide an advantage for cell proliferation.
claims.source: However, the presence of KSHV negatively regulated the transcriptional activity of HIF1α in hypoxic conditions to provide an advantage for cell proliferation compared to KSHV-negative BJAB cells.
claims.evidence: Based on inference from experimental data showing reduced HIF1α activity and sustained proliferation in KSHV-positive cells.

claims.claim: KSHV latent antigens are expressed upon infection and under hypoxic conditions.
claims.source: In addition, it provides new insights into a role for KSHV latent antigens, which was also expressed upon infection as well as under hypoxic conditions, with a major role in this transition.
claims.evidence: Based on established knowledge about KSHV latent antigen expression patterns.

claims.claim: KSHV-encoded LANA, RTA, vGPCR, vCyclin, and vFLIP are well-established antigens expressed during latency, initial infection or under hypoxia induction.
claims.source: The KSHV-encoded LANA, RTA, vGPCR, vCyclin, and vFLIP are well-established antigens expressed during latency, initial infection or under hypoxia induction.
claims.evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about KSHV antigen expression.

claims.claim: Long-term expression of vCyclin is unsuccessful after selection in culture.
claims.source: Further, long-term expression of vCyclin was unsuccessful after selection in culture.
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental observation of vCyclin loss over time.

claims.claim: vCyclin collaborates with HIF1α in mediating its cytosolic translocation and degradation within the lysosomal compartment.
claims.source: These results provide new insights into a role for collaboration of vCyclin with HIF1α in mediating its cytosolic translocation, and the degradation of both vCyclin and HIF1α within the lysosomal compartment.
claims.evidence: Based on inference from multiple experimental observations including colocalization, interaction, and degradation data.

claims.claim: CDK2 mediates HIF1α degradation through the lysosomal pathway.
claims.source: It is important to note that, in KSHV-positive cells, HIF1α itself upregulated expression of vCyclin through HREs transactivation forming a negative feedback control (Figure 7). Adding these finding with already known facts such as CDK2 mediation of HIF1α degradation through lysosomal pathway (Hubbi et al., 2014), and that HIF1α can act as an inhibitor of DNA replication (Hubbi et al., 2013), we can expect to target the phenomenon of lysosomal degradation of HIF1α using Chloroquine to investigate the possible strategy for therapeutic treatment against KSHV-mediated tumorigenesis.
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Hubbi et al., 2014).

claims.claim: HIF1α can act as an inhibitor of DNA replication.

claims.claim: KSHV utilizes a stringently regulated control of HIF1α levels by two of its critical latent antigens for driving the oncogenic phenotype in hypoxia.
claims.source: Overall, the present studies clearly demonstrated that KSHV-encoded vCyclin attenuates HIF1α signaling in a negative feedback loop to create a favorable microenvironment where DNA replication is permitted. The work also explores a new area of investigation as to the role of another oncogenic viral encoded antigen in driving DNA replication in hypoxia. It also extends our knowledge as to the stringent regulation of HIF1α required for KSHV genome replication and cell proliferation by three KSHV-encoded antigens and explores their complementary roles for viral genome persistence and survival of the infected cells in the hypoxic microenvironment.
claims.evidence: Based on inference from the collective experimental findings about vCyclin, LANA, and vGPCR roles.

claims.source: We recently showed that KSHV-encoded-LANA protects replication associated proteins from hypoxia mediated degradation (Singh et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Singh et al., 2019).

claims.claim: Hypoxia induces suppression in transcription, translation, and effects on epigenetic regulation and protein degradation.
claims.source: Other challenging questions behind hypoxic reactivation of KSHV remain unexplained and unexplored. For example, hypoxia also induces suppression in transcription, translation, as well as effects on epigenetic regulation and promotion of protein degradation.

However, we can speculate about the existence of mechanisms that stabilize Cyclins and CDKs under hypoxic conditions in non-infected cells, potentially regulating HIF1α levels in non-infected cells.

results.result: KSHV infection promotes DNA replication in hypoxia while restricting HIF1α transcriptional activity. BJAB-KSHV cells maintain DNA replication under hypoxic conditions despite showing dramatically reduced HIF1α protein levels at 36 hours and compromised upregulation of HIF1α target genes (LDHA, P4HA1, PDK1) compared to KSHV-negative BJAB cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C5 provide converging evidence from multiple experimental approaches (nucleotide analog incorporation, Western blot, real-time PCR) showing that KSHV infection enables DNA replication in hypoxia while restricting HIF1α activity. The data are internally consistent and supported by appropriate controls using isogenic cell lines.

results.result: KSHV-encoded vCyclin specifically restricts HIF1α transcriptional activity under both normoxic and hypoxic conditions. Expression of vCyclin leads to drastic reduction in HIF1α target gene expression, while vGPCR (a known positive regulator of HIF1α) increases target expression as expected.
results.evaluation: Claims C6 and C55 demonstrate specificity of vCyclin's effect through comparison with other KSHV antigens including the positive control vGPCR. Real-time PCR data show consistent reduction in HIF1α targets (LDHA, P4HA1, PDK1) specifically with vCyclin expression.

results.result: vCyclin physically interacts with HIF1α and mediates its cytosolic translocation. vCyclin shows variable subcellular localization (nuclear, cytosolic, or both), colocalizes with HIF1α in multiple compartments, and the interaction is confirmed by immunoprecipitation in both transfected and naturally infected KSHV-positive cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C7-C10, C56-C57 provide multiple lines of evidence (confocal microscopy, immunofluorescence, immunoprecipitation, subcellular fractionation) demonstrating vCyclin-HIF1α interaction and translocation. The findings are validated in both overexpression systems and naturally infected cells (BC3, BCBL1, JSC1).

results.result: vCyclin mediates HIF1α degradation through a non-canonical lysosomal pathway rather than proteasomal degradation. HIF1α levels decrease dose-dependently with vCyclin expression, are protected by chloroquine but not MG132, and HIF1α localizes to lysosomal compartments in vCyclin-expressing cells. This mechanism operates in naturally infected BC3 cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C11-C14, C60-C61, C67-C68 provide strong evidence for lysosomal degradation through pharmacological inhibitor studies, dose-response experiments, colocalization with lysosomal markers, and validation in naturally infected cells. The failure of proteasomal inhibitor MG132 to protect HIF1α while chloroquine provides protection is compelling evidence for the lysosomal pathway.

results.result: HIF1α upregulates vCyclin expression through hypoxia-responsive elements (HREs) in the vCyclin promoter, forming a negative feedback loop. vCyclin transcripts are upregulated in hypoxia in multiple KSHV-positive cell lines, and the first HRE in the vCyclin promoter (LTd) is most responsive to HIF1α.
results.evaluation: Claims C15-C16, C63-C66, C101 demonstrate a feedback regulatory mechanism through real-time PCR, in silico promoter analysis, and luciferase reporter assays. The identification of functional HREs and validation across multiple cell lines (BC3, BCBL1, JSC1) provides strong support for this regulatory circuit.

results.result: HIF1α shows approximately fourfold higher enrichment on the KSHV genome in hypoxia compared to normoxia, but enrichment occurs at regions distinct from the origin of lytic replication (OriLyt). This pattern suggests HIF1α promotes transcription of lytic genes without directly suppressing DNA replication at OriLyt during the examined time period.
results.evaluation: Claims C17-C18, C71-C73 are supported by ChIP-sequencing data from both infected PBMCs and naturally infected BC3 cells. The spatial distribution of HIF1α enrichment away from OriLyt regions is clearly documented, though the interpretation about lack of replication suppression (C72-C73) is inferential and time-dependent.

results.result: Knockdown of vCyclin severely impairs KSHV replication and cell proliferation in hypoxia. BC3-ShvCyclin cells show more than 10-fold reduction in KSHV copy number and replication (measured by SMARD), and are highly compromised for both anchorage-dependent and independent growth. This effect occurs even under normoxic conditions.
results.evaluation: Claims C19-C21, C74-C76 provide functional validation through multiple complementary assays (copy number calculation, SMARD, colony formation, soft agar). The consistency across different readouts and the magnitude of effects (>10-fold reduction) strongly support vCyclin's essential role in KSHV replication and cell proliferation.

results.result: vCyclin expression correlates temporally with HIF1α degradation in naturally infected BC3 cells, and vCyclin itself undergoes degradation over time. GFP-vCyclin levels gradually decrease with almost complete elimination by day 7, and long-term stable expression is unsuccessful.
results.evaluation: Claims C22, C58-C59, C96 document the temporal dynamics of vCyclin and HIF1α through Western blot time courses and microscopy. The observation that vCyclin itself is degraded (possibly through the same lysosomal pathway) adds complexity to the regulatory mechanism and is well-documented experimentally.

results.result: KSHV utilizes vCyclin to balance HIF1α levels through a negative feedback mechanism, enabling DNA replication and proliferation in hypoxia. This represents a stringently regulated control system involving multiple KSHV antigens (vCyclin, LANA, vGPCR) that allows infected cells to bypass hypoxia-mediated replication arrest.
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C49, C76, C97, C102 synthesize the major findings into a coherent mechanistic model. The model is well-supported by the collective experimental evidence showing vCyclin-HIF1α interaction, lysosomal degradation, feedback regulation, and functional consequences of vCyclin knockdown. The integration of multiple KSHV antigens in HIF1α regulation is supported by prior work cited.

results.result: BJAB and BJAB-KSHV cells are validated as isogenic controls through STR profiling and similar passage numbers, and BJAB-KSHV cells show characteristics of latently infected KSHV-positive cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C54, C91 describe essential methodological controls. The use of STR profiling to confirm isogenic background and matching passage numbers addresses potential confounders. These are appropriate quality controls for the experimental system.

results.result: Background information on KSHV biology, including its role as causative agent of KS and association with PEL, MCD, and KICS; genome structure encoding ~90 ORFs including viral homologs; latent vs lytic replication; and functions of major viral proteins (LANA, vCyclin, vFLIP, vIRFs, vGPCR).
results.evaluation: Claims C23-C41 provide established background knowledge supported by appropriate citations to published literature. These claims contextualize the current work but do not represent novel findings from this study.

results.result: Background information on hypoxia biology and HIF1α function, including effects on cellular metabolism, cell cycle arrest, transcriptional targets, and mechanisms of HIF1α regulation through proteasomal and lysosomal degradation pathways.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C45, C52, C69-C70, C77-C83, C89 provide established background on hypoxia and HIF1α biology supported by appropriate citations. These contextualize the significance of KSHV's ability to modulate HIF1α but are not novel findings.

results.result: Background on KSHV-HIF1α interactions, including KSHV's mechanisms to maintain high basal HIF1α levels (through vGPCR/MAPK pathway and LANA-mediated VHL ubiquitination), the paradox of KSHV replication in hypoxia despite elevated HIF1α, and proposals to target HIF1α therapeutically.
results.evaluation: Claims C46-C47, C50-C51, C84-C88, C90 describe prior knowledge about KSHV-HIF1α biology that motivates the current study. These are well-supported by citations and establish the paradox that the current work addresses.

results.result: Interpretive claims about BJAB-KSHV cells being adjusted for growth with higher HIF1α levels, KSHV negatively regulating HIF1α transcriptional activity to provide proliferative advantage, and the role of latent antigens in this process.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C95 represent reasonable inferences from the experimental data showing similar growth patterns despite different HIF1α levels and reduced HIF1α activity in KSHV-positive cells. These interpretations are logical extensions of the data though somewhat speculative.

results.result: Discussion of CDK2-mediated lysosomal degradation of HIF1α, HIF1α as inhibitor of DNA replication, and speculation about using chloroquine to target lysosomal degradation as therapeutic strategy against KSHV tumorigenesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C98-C99 cite established knowledge, but C100 is speculative about therapeutic applications. While the authors demonstrate chloroquine protects HIF1α from degradation, proposing this as a therapeutic strategy is premature without additional validation showing this would inhibit KSHV-mediated oncogenesis. The logic seems counterintuitive since maintaining HIF1α might promote rather than inhibit tumorigenesis.

results.result: Discussion of broader context including LANA's role in protecting replication proteins from hypoxia-mediated degradation, remaining questions about hypoxic reactivation mechanisms, speculation about mechanisms in uninfected cells, and potential implications for other virus-associated cancers.
results.evaluation: Claim C103 cites prior work appropriately. C104 states established knowledge. However, C105-C106 are speculative about mechanisms in uninfected cells and broader implications for other cancers. These speculations are reasonable but lack experimental support in the current study.
